# Nobel Prize in Physics 1921

[![Image 2: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1921/einstein/facts/ [link_17])

Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.

### [Albert Einstein](link_17)

Prize share: 1/1

> The Nobel Prize in Physics 1921 was awarded to Albert Einstein "for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect"

 Albert Einstein received his Nobel Prize one year later, in 1922. During the selection process in 1921, the Nobel Committee for Physics decided that none of the year's nominations met the criteria as outlined in the will of Alfred Nobel. According to the Nobel Foundation's statutes, the Nobel Prize can in such a case be reserved until the following year, and this statute was then applied. Albert Einstein therefore received his Nobel Prize for 1921 one year later, in 1922.

![Image 1: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_0])

Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.

Albert Einstein

 Nobel Prize in Physics 1921

Born: 14 March 1879, Ulm, Germany

Died: 18 April 1955, Princeton, NJ, USA

Affiliation at the time of the award: Kaiser-Wilhelm-Institut (now Max-Planck-Institut) für Physik, Berlin, Germany

Prize motivation: “for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect”

_Albert Einstein received his Nobel Prize one year later, in 1922._

Prize share: 1/1

### Life

Albert Einstein grew up in Munich, where his father founded an electrical engineering company. After studying at the ETH university in Zurich, Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern, during which time he produced several pioneering works in the field of physics. He was later employed at universities in Bern, Zurich, and Prague, and from 1914, in Berlin. After the Nazis seized power in Germany, Einstein immigrated to the US, where he worked at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. Einstein married twice and had three children by his first marriage.

### Work

If metal electrodes are exposed to light, electrical sparks between them occur more readily. For this photoelectric effect to occur, the light waves must be above a certain frequency, however. According to physics theory, the light's intensity should be critical. In one of several epoch-making studies beginning in 1905, Albert Einstein explained that light consists of quanta—packets with fixed energies corresponding to certain frequencies. One such light quantum, a photon, must have a certain minimum frequency before it can liberate an electron.

Six prizes were awarded for achievements that have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind. The 10 laureates' work and discoveries range from optogenetics to efforts to promote peace and international law.

See them all presented here.

## The Nobel Prize in Physics

Awarded the first Nobel Prize in Physics, Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-radiation. This X-ray tube became a frequently used instrument in medicine after this discovery.

© Nobel Media. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

Francis Halzen realised that ice at the South Pole could be used to track particles known as neutrinos. His vision and scientific leadership have been fundamental for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory – a cubic kilometre of ice that is equipped with light sensors. Using IceCube, researchers can capture neutrinos from extremely energy-rich processes in the distant universe.

[Press release](link_0)[Popular information: Ice at the South Pole reveals cosmic particle accelerators](link_1)

[Scientific background](link_2)

[![Image 1: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/press-release/ [link_0])

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 to [Francis Halzen](link_4) “for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.”

Francis Halzen has laid the foundation for an entirely new type of astronomy. His idea was to use glacial ice at the South Pole to capture the secretive particles called neutrinos. The result was the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, which can track neutrinos that originate in the distant cosmos.

[![Image 2: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/summary/ [link_5])

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

> “Francis Halzen has led an international team of researchers and engineers who have provided us with a fantastic instrument. His tenacity and scientific vision has paved the way for a new kind of astronomy.”
> 
> Mark Pearce, Chair of the Nobel Committee for Physics

Have you heard about the IceCube Neutrino Observatory?

### [Albert Einstein](link_19)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1921](link_19)for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.

[![Image 12: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1901/rontgen/ [link_20])

### [Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen](link_20)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1901](link_20)in recognition of the extraordinary services he has rendered by the discovery of the remarkable rays subsequently named after him.

[![Image 13: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2020/ghez/ [link_21])

### [Andrea Ghez](link_21)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 2020](link_21)for the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy.

[![Image 14: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1973/esaki/ [link_22])

### [Leo Esaki](link_22)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1973](link_22)for their experimental discoveries regarding tunneling phenomena in semiconductors and superconductors, respectively.

[![Image 15: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1933/schrodinger/ [link_23])

### [Erwin Schrödinger](link_23)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1933](link_23)for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory.

[![Image 16: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/lhuillier/ [link_24])

### [Anne L’Huillier](link_24)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 2023](link_24)for experimental methods that generate attosecond pulses of light for the study of electron dynamics in matter.

### [Read about Michael Kosterlitz’ battle with MS](link_25)

“I want to take this space to tell any budding scientist that, however bleak the future may seem due to illness or other problems, one cannot say you will not be successful.” Kosterlitz was diagnosed with MS in 1978.

[![Image 17: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2016/kosterlitz/auto-biography/ [link_25])

J. Michael Kosterlitz, Nobel Prize in Physics 2016

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

### [They filled the world with new light](link_26)

Discover how the 2014 physics laureates tamed the unruly semiconductor gallium nitride, paving the way for blue LEDs. This efficient, versatile light source has been a boon to areas without electricity grids.

[![Image 18: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/popular-physicsprize2014-1.pdf [link_26])

The blue LED: an energy- efficient, environmentally-friendly light source

Photo: Public domain

### [The much-anticipated arrival of the Higgs boson](link_27)

Read what caused the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences to exclaim, “Here, at last!” The Higgs particle completed the Standard Model of particle physics which describes building blocks of the universe.

[![Image 19: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/popular-physicsprize2013-1.pdf [link_27])

Portrait of Peter Higgs, during a visit to CERN in 2008

© CERN 2008. Photo: Claudia Marcelloni

Nobel Prize in Physics 1901

The very first Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Wilhelm Röntgen for his discovery of X-rays. They are still used to diagnose bone fractures, locate embedded bullets and more.

[![Image 20: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1901/speedread/ [link_28])

Credit: Wellcome Collection.

Nobel Prize in Physics 2009

The charge-coupled device invented by Willard Boyle and George Smith was a breakthrough for digital camera technology, and continues to play a crucial role for scientific imaging.

[![Image 21: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/stories/can-you-imagine-life-without-these-discoveries/#ccd [link_29])

Group of cameras on tripod during photographing urban skyline at twlight. View from Elephant Mountain in Taipei.

Credit: Jaromir/Getty Images

## The Nobel Prize in Physics

Awarded the first Nobel Prize in Physics, Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-radiation. This X-ray tube became a frequently used instrument in medicine after this discovery.

© Nobel Media. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

Francis Halzen realised that ice at the South Pole could be used to track particles known as neutrinos. His vision and scientific leadership have been fundamental for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory – a cubic kilometre of ice that is equipped with light sensors. Using IceCube, researchers can capture neutrinos from extremely energy-rich processes in the distant universe.

[Press release](link_0)[Popular information: Ice at the South Pole reveals cosmic particle accelerators](link_1)

[Scientific background](link_2)

[![Image 1: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/press-release/ [link_0])

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 to [Francis Halzen](link_4) “for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.”

Francis Halzen has laid the foundation for an entirely new type of astronomy. His idea was to use glacial ice at the South Pole to capture the secretive particles called neutrinos. The result was the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, which can track neutrinos that originate in the distant cosmos.

[![Image 2: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/summary/ [link_5])

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

> “Francis Halzen has led an international team of researchers and engineers who have provided us with a fantastic instrument. His tenacity and scientific vision has paved the way for a new kind of astronomy.”
> 
> Mark Pearce, Chair of the Nobel Committee for Physics

![Image 1: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)
Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.
Albert Einstein
Nobel Prize in Physics 1921
Born: 14 March 1879, Ulm, Germany
Died: 18 April 1955, Princeton, NJ, USA
Affiliation at the time of the award: Kaiser-Wilhelm-Institut (now Max-Planck-Institut) für Physik, Berlin, Germany
Prize motivation: “for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect”
_Albert Einstein received his Nobel Prize one year later, in 1922._
Prize share: 1/1

### Life
Albert Einstein grew up in Munich, where his father founded an electrical engineering company. After studying at the ETH university in Zurich, Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern, during which time he produced several pioneering works in the field of physics. He was later employed at universities in Bern, Zurich, and Prague, and from 1914, in Berlin. After the Nazis seized power in Germany, Einstein immigrated to the US, where he worked at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. Einstein married twice and had three children by his first marriage.

### Work
If metal electrodes are exposed to light, electrical sparks between them occur more readily. For this photoelectric effect to occur, the light waves must be above a certain frequency, however. According to physics theory, the light's intensity should be critical. In one of several epoch-making studies beginning in 1905, Albert Einstein explained that light consists of quanta—packets with fixed energies corresponding to certain frequencies. One such light quantum, a photon, must have a certain minimum frequency before it can liberate an electron.
Six prizes were awarded for achievements that have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind. The 10 laureates' work and discoveries range from optogenetics to efforts to promote peace and international law.
See them all presented here.

Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.

Albert Einstein

 Nobel Prize in Physics 1921

Born: 14 March 1879, Ulm, Germany

Died: 18 April 1955, Princeton, NJ, USA

Affiliation at the time of the award: Kaiser-Wilhelm-Institut (now Max-Planck-Institut) für Physik, Berlin, Germany

Prize motivation: “for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect”

_Albert Einstein received his Nobel Prize one year later, in 1922._

Prize share: 1/1

### Life

Albert Einstein grew up in Munich, where his father founded an electrical engineering company. After studying at the ETH university in Zurich, Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern, during which time he produced several pioneering works in the field of physics. He was later employed at universities in Bern, Zurich, and Prague, and from 1914, in Berlin. After the Nazis seized power in Germany, Einstein immigrated to the US, where he worked at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. Einstein married twice and had three children by his first marriage.

### Work

If metal electrodes are exposed to light, electrical sparks between them occur more readily. For this photoelectric effect to occur, the light waves must be above a certain frequency, however. According to physics theory, the light's intensity should be critical. In one of several epoch-making studies beginning in 1905, Albert Einstein explained that light consists of quanta—packets with fixed energies corresponding to certain frequencies. One such light quantum, a photon, must have a certain minimum frequency before it can liberate an electron.

Six prizes were awarded for achievements that have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind. The 10 laureates' work and discoveries range from optogenetics to efforts to promote peace and international law.

See them all presented here.

## The Nobel Prize in Physics

Awarded the first Nobel Prize in Physics, Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-radiation. This X-ray tube became a frequently used instrument in medicine after this discovery.

© Nobel Media. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

Francis Halzen realised that ice at the South Pole could be used to track particles known as neutrinos. His vision and scientific leadership have been fundamental for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory – a cubic kilometre of ice that is equipped with light sensors. Using IceCube, researchers can capture neutrinos from extremely energy-rich processes in the distant universe.

[Press release](link_0)[Popular information: Ice at the South Pole reveals cosmic particle accelerators](link_1)

[Scientific background](link_2)

[![Image 1: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/press-release/ [link_0])

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 to [Francis Halzen](link_4) “for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.”

Francis Halzen has laid the foundation for an entirely new type of astronomy. His idea was to use glacial ice at the South Pole to capture the secretive particles called neutrinos. The result was the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, which can track neutrinos that originate in the distant cosmos.

[![Image 2: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/summary/ [link_5])

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

> “Francis Halzen has led an international team of researchers and engineers who have provided us with a fantastic instrument. His tenacity and scientific vision has paved the way for a new kind of astronomy.”
> 
> Mark Pearce, Chair of the Nobel Committee for Physics

Have you heard about the IceCube Neutrino Observatory?

## The mysterious neutrino

The detection of cosmic neutrinos.

High hopes for neutrino astronomy.

Read Frederick Reines Nobel Prize lecture.

Understanding the elusive elementary particle.

[![Image 11: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1921/einstein/ [link_19])

### [Albert Einstein](link_19)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1921](link_19)for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.

[![Image 12: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1901/rontgen/ [link_20])

### [Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen](link_20)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1901](link_20)in recognition of the extraordinary services he has rendered by the discovery of the remarkable rays subsequently named after him.

[![Image 13: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2020/ghez/ [link_21])

### [Andrea Ghez](link_21)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 2020](link_21)for the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy.

[![Image 14: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1973/esaki/ [link_22])

### [Leo Esaki](link_22)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1973](link_22)for their experimental discoveries regarding tunneling phenomena in semiconductors and superconductors, respectively.

[![Image 15: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1933/schrodinger/ [link_23])

### [Erwin Schrödinger](link_23)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1933](link_23)for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory.

[![Image 16: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/lhuillier/ [link_24])

### [Anne L’Huillier](link_24)

[Nobel Prize in Physics 2023](link_24)for experimental methods that generate attosecond pulses of light for the study of electron dynamics in matter.

### [Read about Michael Kosterlitz’ battle with MS](link_25)

“I want to take this space to tell any budding scientist that, however bleak the future may seem due to illness or other problems, one cannot say you will not be successful.” Kosterlitz was diagnosed with MS in 1978.

[![Image 17: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2016/kosterlitz/auto-biography/ [link_25])

J. Michael Kosterlitz, Nobel Prize in Physics 2016

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

### [They filled the world with new light](link_26)

Discover how the 2014 physics laureates tamed the unruly semiconductor gallium nitride, paving the way for blue LEDs. This efficient, versatile light source has been a boon to areas without electricity grids.

[![Image 18: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/popular-physicsprize2014-1.pdf [link_26])

The blue LED: an energy- efficient, environmentally-friendly light source

Photo: Public domain

### [The much-anticipated arrival of the Higgs boson](link_27)

Read what caused the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences to exclaim, “Here, at last!” The Higgs particle completed the Standard Model of particle physics which describes building blocks of the universe.

[![Image 19: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/popular-physicsprize2013-1.pdf [link_27])

Portrait of Peter Higgs, during a visit to CERN in 2008

© CERN 2008. Photo: Claudia Marcelloni

Nobel Prize in Physics 1901

The very first Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Wilhelm Röntgen for his discovery of X-rays. They are still used to diagnose bone fractures, locate embedded bullets and more.

[![Image 20: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1901/speedread/ [link_28])

Credit: Wellcome Collection.

Nobel Prize in Physics 2009

The charge-coupled device invented by Willard Boyle and George Smith was a breakthrough for digital camera technology, and continues to play a crucial role for scientific imaging.

[![Image 21: Cameras](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_3])](https://www.nobelprize.org/stories/can-you-imagine-life-without-these-discoveries/#ccd [link_29])

Group of cameras on tripod during photographing urban skyline at twlight. View from Elephant Mountain in Taipei.

Credit: Jaromir/Getty Images

Join thousands of global subscribers enjoying the free monthly Nobel Prize highlights, trivia and up-to-date information.

Original direct_answer chunk 1:
### Life
Albert Einstein grew up in Munich, where his father founded an electrical engineering company. After studying at the ETH university in Zurich, Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern, during which time he produced several pioneering works in the field of physics. He was later employed at universities in Bern, Zurich, and Prague, and from 1914, in Berlin. After the Nazis seized power in Germany, Einstein immigrated to the US, where he worked at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. Einstein married twice and had three children by his first marriage.

texts.1:
### Life
Albert Einstein grew up in Munich, where his father founded an electrical engineering company. After studying at the ETH university in Zurich, Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern, during which time he produced several pioneering works in the field of physics. He was later employed at universities in Bern, Zurich, and Prague, and from 1914, in Berlin. After the Nazis seized power in Germany, Einstein immigrated to the US, where he worked at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. Einstein married twice and had three children by his first marriage.
texts.2:
### Work
If metal electrodes are exposed to light, electrical sparks between them occur more readily. For this photoelectric effect to occur, the light waves must be above a certain frequency, however. According to physics theory, the light's intensity should be critical. In one of several epoch-making studies beginning in 1905, Albert Einstein explained that light consists of quanta—packets with fixed energies corresponding to certain frequencies. One such light quantum, a photon, must have a certain minimum frequency before it can liberate an electron.
Six prizes were awarded for achievements that have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind. The 10 laureates' work and discoveries range from optogenetics to efforts to promote peace and international law.
